content.thinking:
I'm planning to write the full file carefully in one pass without testing, designing a scythe displayed upright on a small plinth, with the shaft resting vertically and the blade curving at the top, roughly 2 meters tall overall.

For the skeleton, I only need joints for the moving parts, so I'll set up a root "plinth" joint, a "shaft" joint, and a short hanging chain of "charm" joints for dangling trinkets. Stylistically I'm going for a League of Legends look: exaggerated dynamic shapes, bone ivory and dark purple-black metal, with teal glow accents and gold trim. I'm blocking out the plinth as a stepped octagonal lathe base with a glowing teal rune ring, then sweeping the shaft with a slight S-curve from the base up to the top, giving it a bone-like texture with vertebra segments and grip wraps, before shaping the blade extending outward from the top.

Now I'm plotting the crescent blade's outline as a series of 2D points forming the spine and cutting edge in the XY plane, extending outward from the top of the shaft toward +X with a sharp curved tip.

Still plotting leaf coordinates...

I'm deciding to keep the near-tip corners unsharp despite risk, then moving to painting: I want a cel-shaded gradient from ivory to teal near the edge, plus a separate glowing teal strip swept along the edge's catmull points to give it a luminous inner-edge effect.

For the blade material, I'm going with ivory bone coloring with a dark purple-black rim near the spine and teal glow veins, approximating the spine curve with piecewise linear interpolation so I can measure distance from it for the rim shading and rib striping.

Now I'm planning bone spikes along the spine, computing tangent and normal vectors from the catmull-rom path samples so each spike juts outward and slightly leans back toward the hub.

For the hub itself, I'm designing a dragon skull motif—stretched ivory sphere forming the cranium, a forward-facing snout, swept-back horns, glowing teal eye sockets, small cone teeth, and a jaw piece, with the blade emerging from the jaws for that LoL-style flair.

Below the grip, I'm adding a hanging chain of soul charms off a ring on the shaft: three joints forming a rope-like cord using a catmull path with two spans, ending in a lathe-built glowing soul-wisp teardrop as the tip.

Now I'm setting up the base joint and making sure every other part explicitly binds to it rather than letting nearby charm joints steal them, using a small helper function to assign the base bone to all parts and sweeps by default.

Then I'm shaping the plinth with a lathe outline resting at y=0, keeping colors under the 64-count limit since cel paints don't count, and adding a glowing teal rune ring near the top made from a swept catmull circle.

Now I'm adding floating soul wisps—small glowing teal spheres with tail cones orbiting the plinth—plus a gold ferrule cylinder and four curved bone-claw feet gripping the shaft base, generated with a loop around the ring.

Shaft curve with painted banding...

I'll simplify by making the shaft perfectly straight vertically instead of following a curved sweep, placing knuckle rings at intervals while skipping the grip zone.

Now I'm adding gold cylinder rings at the grip ends and shaping the skull head at the top of the staff using scaled ellipsoids for the cranium, with a frustum box for the snout and a lower jaw piece to follow.

Still placing teeth cones...

Now I'm adding glowing eye spheres with dark eye sockets, and sweeping back dramatic horn shapes with bezier curves tapering from thick base to pointed tip.

Adding more horn and skull geometry...

Still defining spur and blade edge points...

Mapping out the rune placement coordinates on the blade...

Converting the midline points to SVG coordinates and sketching a smooth curved path through them using bezier segments to approximate the rune's centerline.

Adding gold collar lathe geometry and a glowing gem socket, then surrounding it with a ring of small curved claws gripping the gem, plus a charm cord attachment point along the shaft.

Setting up the joint hierarchy with the base and chain charms, then placing seven glowing floating motes around the plinth using a deterministic sine-based formula for position, each with a downward teal taper spike for a flame-like trail.

I'm also adding a flat rune circle texture plane on top of the plinth, sized to fit the lathe profile, with concentric rings, tick marks, and glyphs for a magical inscription look.

Now I'm defining the color palette: bone whites, deep purples, golds, and teal accents, with darker variants for shading.

I'm working out the plinth material with mottled purple patches for texture, and setting up the lathe geometry parameters before moving into the extrude API.

I'm defining the blade extrusion with proper thickness direction and bevel, then writing a spine-based paint function that darkens the center seam versus edges to give the blade shape depth.

Still writing paint logic...

Adding the straight shaft rod and sketching a paint function for banded coloring along it...

Still working through the knob spheres, plinth base, and horn sweep geometry with their color bands...

Now I'm placing the brow ridge and cheek spikes with specific directions and lengths, then shaping the skull cranium as a scaled sphere with a snout box extending forward.

For the eye sockets, I'm positioning dark purple sphere sockets with smaller glowing eye spheres offset outward, skipping jaw joint details since the weapon takes priority there. For the collar, I'm using a lathe shape painted gold, working out the vertical placement so it sits just below the skull's bottom edge with a gem accent.

Now I'm placing a glowing gem sphere on the collar's front and deciding to put claws only at the base rather than ringing the collar. For the base claws, I'm working out a four-fold radial arrangement using curved bezier sweeps from a wide base near the shaft outward to narrow tips.

Adding the gold ferrule lathe shape...

I'm double-checking imports and TypeScript strictness to avoid unused-variable errors, confirming that path and tangent sampling return Vector3 objects, and starting to lay out the charm's chain using a catmull curve through a few control points.

For the chain I'm naming the joints charm1/charm2/charm3 so the hinge spans map correctly, then sweeping leather-colored tubes along it. For the hanging wisp, I'm falling back to the last joint if the chain's tip reference is undefined, then lathing its outline so it dangles downward from that point.

Still writing lathe and glow code...
